result.title: Vulnerability Analysis for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement
result.summary: Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (SMARL) aims to learn cooperative control policies under prescribed safety constraints. Al- though existing SMARL methods focus on enforcing safety during policy optimization, their vulnerability remains largely unexplored. This paper investigates inference-time observation attacks against SMARL, where an adversary perturbs the observations of a subset of agents, thereby altering the actions produced by their policies. We propose MinMax Attack, an attack framework that jointly selects adversarial target actions for compromised agents while accounting for the Cooperative Resistance of benign agents. We further derive a bound on the induced safety cost and characterize its relation- ship with the Compromised-Agent Budget and the Perturbation Budget. Experiments across multiple safety-critical multi-agent benchmarks and representative state-of-the-art SMARL algorithms show that MinMax Attack induces substantially higher safety costs than existing attack baselines while preserving task reward, thereby reducing its detectability and achieving both attack effectiveness and stealthiness.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究安全多智能体强化学习在推理阶段的观测攻击，提出 MinMax Attack：联合为被攻陷智能体选取对抗目标动作并计入其余智能体的协同抵抗，同时推导安全代价上界并刻画其与受控智能体预算、扰动预算的关系，在多类安全关键基准上验证攻击更隐蔽且安全代价更高。
